answer: Cap agents per human, not per key. Each agent registers with a zero-knowledge proof from a one-per-person credential that reveals only a nullifier, a hash that repeats if the same person tries a fourth agent, so the ledger refuses it without learning who they are. A farm can wander from key to key, but every key lands on the same island of three slots. Past that, each fake needs another real person's credential, rented at maybe $20 each (illustrative), so cost grows linearly. Like a lotus, the person stays below the surface while the count shows above.
